outcome: mean costs per pregnancy (women and neonates)
cohort: The study included 30,924 singleton, cephalic, and term live births (37-40 weeks gestation) in public hospitals of Queensland, Australia, between 2016 and 2018, excluding those with previous cesarean birth, no labor, or specific maternal conditions.
finding: The mean costs per pregnancy (combined women and neonates) were consistently higher for induction of labor compared with expectant management at each week of gestation (37-40), regardless of parity, primarily driven by maternal inpatient admissions.
mod_finding: The findings support previous evidence of higher cesarean rates after induction of labor, suggesting higher costs are likely due to the intervention itself rather than underlying maternal risk.
followup_time: during the month of labor and birth
